source.title: Inductive Bias of Multi-Channel Linear Convolutional Networks with Bounded Weight Norm
source.authors: Meena Jagadeesan; Ilya P. Razenshteyn; Suriya Gunasekar

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether output-channel count and kernel size affect weight-norm complexity in gradient-descent-trained convolutional networks, using weight norms and learned predictors rather than held-out generalization error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training loss and representation-cost estimates, learned predictors, and theoretical regularizer results, but does not report held-out test error or a train–test generalization gap. Results cited from prior work are not cataloged as this study's own rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures induced weight-norm regularizers and learned predictor structure, not held-out accuracy, test error, or generalization gaps. Its width and architecture results therefore do not test V2 or V3, and it reports no results testing the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, channel-count invariance is proved for all C ≥ 1 with single-channel inputs and for C ≥ RK with multiple input channels; C ≥ R is conjectured generally. Experiments support approximate invariance of estimated representation costs on linear MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks and some MNIST ReLU networks. Kernel size changes the induced regularizer and predictor structure. The authors do not conclude that these results establish held-out generalization performance.
record.recipe_differences: Studies induced weight-norm regularization and its relation to gradient descent; does not test held-out generalization. Uses small, linearly separable binary subsets and estimated parameter norms.
record.method_sensitivity: Estimated regularizer varies with kernel size and, for three-input-channel CIFAR-10, with output-channel count below 3. Padding choice is also varied. The authors report ReLU outliers and summarize those results by medians.

fits_no_version.finding: For two-layer linear convolutional networks, the induced regularizer is independent of output-channel count for single-channel inputs; for multiple input channels, invariance is proved when C ≥ RK and conjectured when C ≥ R. Experiments approximately support the latter threshold, including MNIST ReLU experiments summarized by medians.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing convolutional width can leave the minimum weight-norm representation cost and estimated norm of learned predictors approximately unchanged. This does not establish how test error changes with width.

fits_no_version.finding: Kernel size changes the induced regularizer and learned predictor structure; larger kernels promote Fourier sparsity in the reported linear-network experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional kernel size affects function-space inductive bias under weight-norm minimization, without establishing a convolutional advantage in held-out accuracy.

record.problems: The experiments use small training subsets and report no held-out test error. The induced regularizer is approximated by trained weight norms, which the authors state are only upper bounds; some values are summarized by medians after outliers. ReLU experiments exceed the paper's theoretical scope.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the study's experimental outcomes concern estimated induced regularizers and predictors, not the claim's held-out error or generalization gap. Figures and tables reporting those outcomes are therefore not cataloged as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required to fit the training data.
Held-out error comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks, including local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate, and the record explicitly declares the regularizer and predictor results as omitted. Its tests/T2 classification should be corrected because these outcomes measure a related construct outside all eight versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label generalization.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons on held-out performance.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
